scope: One existing source and five existing recipes: physical and exposure follow-up; selected extraction, not complete paper

source.version: Same SHA256 as preceding batch; publisher-formatted university copy with overlapping review/final text. Table pages 11/12/15 are visually legible.
source.rawRetention: Temporary scratch PDF/renderings only; no raw source in public Git or CI artifacts

deduplication.relationship: Supersedes pending Table 3/4/5 extraction states in recipes-biochar-2026-10-15.json; original audit remains historical.

review.firstPass: Web PDF text and local pdftotext; rows, columns, units and methods mapped
review.secondPass: Primary-agent visual inspection of all 40 selected cells on rendered pages 11,12,15 at 1500px; extremes, minus/plus signs, spread values and method chronology checked
review.statusCheck: Exact DOI correction/retraction and publisher searches on 16 October; not comprehensive status clearance

inventoryUpdates.state: All 5 rows × 4 quantity columns source-checked; 10 reported spreads retained; consistency author-calculated
All five previously pending 28-day dynamic moduli checked with spreads; prior 15 compression results unchanged
All 5 rows × 3 columns checked; 10 reported spreads; five signed author-rounded changes retained

conditions: Fresh spread uses two perpendicular diameter readings, not n=2 specimens
Physical samples: method specifies three 27×40mm cylinders; 28-day cure then about 3-day immersion and at least 2-day 40°C drying; actual total test age unassigned
Capillary/exposed samples: three 27×55mm cylinders; 28d cure +8d capillary exposure +4d 40°C drying =40d; §3 alternatively describes constant-weight endpoint
Dynamic modulus is ultrasonic, not static Young’s modulus
Atmospheric water absorption is distinct from capillary uptake
No matched unexposed 40-day control; no causal separation of age/water/heating
± type unresolved; method-specified n is not confirmed valid-result count
bounds: Characterization kept outside ordinary strength result array and goal planner
No own measurement inserted into notebook; short source notes retained within v1 3000-character bound
No figure digitization, assays, supplier availability, general optimum or durability qualification
Canonical bibliography and pilot counts unchanged; no new independent dataset

context.label: Fresh paste
context.ageOrigin: Immediately after preparation
context.specimen: Brass truncated cone: diameters 20–40 mm, height 60 mm
context.method: §2.3.1: remove mould and average two perpendicular spread diameters. C = 100 × (dm − 40)/40. Two diameter readings are not independent specimens.

context.label: 28-day cure, then physical-test conditioning
context.ageOrigin: Curing duration before conditioning; not total test age
context.specimen: Three cylinders per recipe, 27 mm diameter × 40 mm height (§2.2)
context.method: §2.3.2: EN 772-13 bulk density and EN 772-21 atmospheric-pressure water absorption. After 28-day cure: immerse about 3 days, weigh wet and hydrostatically, then dry at 40 °C at least 2 days. Repeat weighings until mass changes <2%. This is not capillary uptake or sorptivity.

context.label: 28-day initial dynamic modulus
context.ageOrigin: Initial curing age
context.specimen: Cylinders, 27 mm diameter × 55 mm height
context.method: §2.3.4: Matest C369N ultrasonic pulse velocity tester, EN 12504-4, before compression. Dynamic modulus is not static Young’s modulus; per-age replicate count unresolved.

context.label: 40-day total age after capillary exposure and drying
context.ageOrigin: 28 days cure + 8 days capillary exposure + 4 days drying
context.specimen: Three cylinders per recipe, 27 mm diameter × 55 mm height (§2.3.4)
context.method: §§2.3.2/2.3.4: EN 15801 capillary setup on filter paper over shallow water, then 40 °C oven. Compression: Wolpert 100 kN, 5 mm/min, EN 196-1 except specimen dimensions. Dynamic modulus: Matest C369N, EN 12504-4, before compression. §3 describes drying to constant mass; §2.3.4 specifies four days. No matched unexposed 40-day control is reported; age, water and heating effects cannot be separated.
